0.title: All in order
0.detail: Alfred reports no fault. The box is clean, calm, and standing by.

1.title: Something needs a look
1.detail: Alfred has flagged a fault but has not named it. It is holding position until the matter is resolved.
1.action: Check Alfred's status ring and the app for the specific condition, then clear it as advised.

DFS.title: The waste drawer is full
DFS.detail: The drawer has reached capacity and Alfred will not run another cycle until it is emptied.
DFS.action: Slide out the drawer, tie off and dispose of the liner, seat a fresh one, and return the drawer until it clicks.

SDF.title: The waste drawer was full at startup
SDF.detail: Alfred woke to find the drawer already at capacity, so it declined to cycle.
SDF.action: Empty the drawer and re-seat it; Alfred will resume its duties once it reports clear.

BR.title: The bonnet has been removed
BR.detail: The globe bonnet is off or not seated squarely, so Alfred has paused for safety.
BR.action: Refit the bonnet, aligning the tabs, and press until it settles flush before resuming.

CSF.title: The cat sensor is troubled
CSF.detail: Alfred's weight sensor is reporting an implausible reading and cannot confirm the globe is clear.
CSF.action: Ensure nothing is resting on or against the unit, wipe the base contacts, and let Alfred re-tare on a level floor.

PD.title: Pinch guard tripped — something is in the path
PD.detail: Alfred detected an obstruction at the globe opening and stopped the cycle at once to keep your companion safe.
PD.action: Clear anything caught in the opening, confirm the coast is clear, and Alfred will carry on.

SCF.title: The globe motor has stalled
SCF.detail: The cleaning globe could not turn freely; Alfred halted the motor to avoid strain.
SCF.action: Remove the bonnet and globe, clear any clumped litter or debris binding the rollers, refit, and resume.

OTF.title: Motor over-torque
OTF.detail: The globe drew more force than expected while turning — usually a jam or an overfilled globe.
OTF.action: Reduce the litter to the fill line, check for hardened clumps around the rim, then start a fresh cycle.

SPF.title: Motor under-torque
SPF.detail: The globe turned with less resistance than expected, which can mean a slipped or disengaged drive.
SPF.action: Reseat the globe firmly on its drive collar and confirm it rotates smoothly by hand before resuming.

DHF.title: Drawer sensor (DFI) needs cleaning
DHF.detail: The drawer-full indicator's laser is obscured, so Alfred cannot judge how full the drawer is.
DHF.action: Wipe the small laser window and its facing sensor inside the drawer bay with a dry cloth, then re-seat the drawer.

DPF.title: Drawer position fault
DPF.detail: Alfred cannot confirm the waste drawer is closed and latched.
DPF.action: Open the drawer fully, clear the runners of stray litter, and slide it home until it clicks.

HPF.title: Hall / position sensor fault
HPF.detail: A globe-position sensor is not reporting, so Alfred cannot verify where the globe has stopped.
HPF.action: Power-cycle Alfred at the wall for ten seconds; if the fault returns, the unit needs service.

OFF.title: Alfred is offline
OFF.detail: The unit has dropped off the network and is not reporting its condition.
OFF.action: Confirm Alfred has power, check the Wi-Fi and its DHCP reservation, then wait for it to rejoin.

OFFLINE.title: Alfred has lost its Wi-Fi
OFFLINE.detail: The connection to Alfred has lapsed; the last known state may be stale.
OFFLINE.action: Verify the router is up and Alfred is on the expected network; restore the link and telemetry will resume.

USB.title: Power / USB fault
USB.detail: Alfred is reporting an unstable supply or a USB accessory fault.
USB.action: Seat the power adapter firmly in the wall and the unit, avoid extension leads, and unplug any suspect USB accessory.

0.title: At your service
0.detail: Alfred is ready and awaiting your command.

1.title: Just a moment
1.detail: Alfred is briefly occupied and not ready for that request yet. It will free itself shortly.
1.action: Wait a few seconds and try again.

CCP.title: Cleaning cycle in progress
CCP.detail: Alfred is mid-cycle, tidying the globe. New commands wait until it finishes.
CCP.action: Give it a moment — the cycle runs for well under two minutes.

CCC.title: Cycle just finished — settling
CCC.detail: Alfred has completed a clean and is settling back to ready. This clears on its own.
CCC.action: No action needed; Alfred will present itself as ready momentarily.

EC.title: Emptying the globe
EC.detail: Alfred is running an empty cycle to clear the globe. It cannot take other commands until done.
EC.action: Let the empty cycle finish, then proceed.

P.title: Cycle paused
P.detail: The cleaning cycle is paused — often because a presence was sensed near the globe.
P.action: Once the coast is clear, resume the cycle or wait for Alfred to continue on its own.

CD.title: A guest has been detected
CD.detail: Alfred sensed your companion in or near the globe and is politely waiting before it cycles.
CD.action: No action needed — Alfred will proceed once its guest has departed.

CSI.title: Cat sensor interrupted — holding
CSI.detail: The weight sensor was interrupted, so Alfred is holding the cycle out of courtesy.
CSI.action: Give it a moment; Alfred resumes automatically once the sensor settles.

CST.title: Cat sensor timing
CST.detail: Alfred is running its post-visit timer before cycling, so the litter has a moment to settle.
CST.action: No action needed — the cycle will begin shortly.

PWRU.title: Powering up
PWRU.detail: Alfred is starting and running its self-check before it accepts commands.
PWRU.action: Wait for the status ring to settle to ready.

SLEEP.title: Alfred is resting
SLEEP.detail: The unit is in its scheduled sleep window and will not cycle until it wakes.
SLEEP.action: Wait for the sleep window to end, or adjust the schedule if you need it active now.
